ctx.x: As I say, not because she's my daughter. She's smart. I've heard so many people say how smart she was.

Let me put, this is real too, and we're interviewing Mr. and Mrs. AC Senegal. It's May the 24th, 1962 Thursday. And I'm looking at this piece of sheet music. I see it's copyrighted 1924. That's right. Is that right? And it's got a picture of your daughter. Imelda Serena Robinson. And the music is by J. Charles McNeil. Is that a local McNeil? No, he's from, I think he's from California. He must have been a very talented lady to write this. And they recorded some of her, one of her songs. Was this song they…

I'm going to look at that record. I have a record here. And she was dying over. But her husband said, oh, Mrs. Senegal, don't rush her. Don't push her with this. Because I need her with these children. More than that, you know? So I, you know, she'd write to me. And mother, do this, write to the, I wouldn't. I said, no.
